Subject: PoC: erasure evidence scope and acceptance checklist

Hi Rachel / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aurum Health is comfortable running the small PoC but we need to lock the evidence that will meet our privacy sign-off. Attached is a starting checklist (poc-checklist.xlsx) from our privacy lead. High level asks: 

- What specific documentary outputs will Redwood provide at PoC completion (e.g., audit log export, manifest, signed certificate)?
- Do backups and KV caches get included in the evidence bundle or are they carved out?
- How will you demonstrate deletion from replicas that live in third-party cloud backups?

Can you confirm these points and propose an acceptance timeline so we can align our internal legal review? We are aiming for an EU-in-scope PoC next week.

Thanks,
Marco

Subject: Re: PoC: erasure evidence scope and acceptance checklist

Marco — thanks for the clear checklist. Below is what Redwood can commit to for the PoC evidence bundle and a proposed acceptance workflow. I copied Laura and Jonas for ops/legal alignment.

Summary of deliverables (PoC final bundle):
- Audit log extract (CSV) covering request IDs, timestamps, user/client ID, action type (DELETE/ERASE), and resulting status.
- Erasure manifest (JSON & human-readable PDF) listing objects targeted for deletion, timestamps of server-side deletion, and tombstone markers.
- Signed attestation (PDF) from Redwood Security that the requested objects were removed from the primary serving layer and KV cache within the stated window.
- Snapshot sampling evidence: when feasible, a sample query on a snapshot taken post-erasure to show absent records (limited for PoC).
- Operational checklist sign-off from Redwood Ops confirming the playbook steps were executed.

Carveouts and scope notes:
- Backups: for PoC we will provide a documented backup-handling statement and a manifest of backup locations. Full backup restoration verification is out-of-scope for the PoC unless Aurum wants to fund an extended verification run.
- Replication/third-party cloud backups: we will produce logs showing delete propagation attempts and retention tombstone timestamps; if backups are managed entirely by a cloud provider (e.g., snapshot-level archival), we will provide our deletion request timestamps and the provider-facing ticket/confirmation where available.
- KV caches: active KV caches will be flushed and evidence recorded; ephemeral caches that are naturally expired will be documented in the playbook.

Acceptance workflow proposal:
1) Redwood delivers the evidence bundle and ops checklist to Aurum (Day 0).
2) Aurum runs a simple 48-hour review window and requests clarifying items (Day 0–2).
3) If clarifications do not materially change the deletion result, Aurum signs the PoC acceptance form.

Proposed timeline: we can deliver the bundle within 3 business days after you confirm the exact object set for erasure.

Links and attachments:
- Redwood PoC evidence guide (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AruM-PoC-Samples

Next steps: please confirm the object set and whether you need backup restoration verification. If you accept the proposed carveouts, we'll prepare the PoC bundle and include the attestation.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Subject: Re: PoC: erasure evidence scope and acceptance checklist

Quick operational note — adding ops context so the acceptance criteria map to actionable steps for the runbook.

- We will flush active KV caches and record TTL flush times (log entry + step ID).
- For backups: our standard process is to attach a deletion request to the provider snapshot tag; we record provider ticket IDs where the provider issues one. For providers that do not issue explicit deletion confirmations, we provide timestamps and our initiated ticket.
- Replica consistency: some replicas are eventual; we will include the propagation window. For the PoC, we recommend Aurum accept propagation evidence rather than full provider snapshot inspection.

I'll attach the ops playbook excerpt to the PoC bundle (ops-erase-playbook.pdf). If legal needs a stronger guarantee on backups, we should discuss a scoped addendum.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@aurumhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC: erasure evidence scope and acceptance checklist

Thanks Rachel and Jonas — this is helpful. Two follow-ups from our privacy/legal team after internal review: 

1) Onshore trigger: Aurum's policy requires that when deletion is requested for EU-resident data and the backup or replica resides outside the EU, an onshore-handling option must be available (either: proof of deletion from an EU-hosted copy, or transfer of the backup object to an EU jurisdiction prior to deletion). Can Redwood confirm whether you can provide a proof path for onshore-handling or if the only option is to rely on provider logs?

2) Evidence granularity: our legal team prefers a signed manifest that includes object-level identifiers (or hashed identifiers) rather than sampling. Is Redwood able to produce a hashed-ID manifest for PoC? If not, we need to schedule an extended run.

I've attached our evidence matrix with preferred fields for acceptance (evidence-matrix.csv).

Marco

Subject: Re: PoC: erasure evidence scope and acceptance checklist

Marco — thanks for the precision. Responses below and final action items for the PoC.

1) Onshore-handling / cross-border backups:
- For the PoC we can provide one of two tracks: (A) proof-of-deletion from an EU-hosted replica (if Aurum designates an EU object set for the PoC) OR (B) a provider-ticket-backed timeline showing when Redwood issued deletion and when the provider acknowledged the request.
- We cannot in the PoC move third-party backups between jurisdictions (that would need an operational project and likely data-migration costs). If Aurum requires jurisdictional movement prior to deletion that is out-of-scope for the standard PoC.

2) Hashed manifest: yes — we can produce an object-level hashed-ID manifest (SHA-256) that lists the hashed identifiers of every object requested for deletion. This will be included in the PoC bundle. For transparency we will also include the mapping procedure (how you can reproduce the hashes from your own export).

Updated acceptance items (to be included in PoC bundle):
- Full hashed-ID manifest (SHA-256) for the requested object set.
- Audit log extract with correlated deletion request IDs.
- Signed attestation from Redwood Security.
- Provider ticket IDs for backup-related deletion requests (where available).
- Ops playbook excerpt and a short sampling report for snapshot checks.

Timeline and next steps:
- If Aurum confirms track (A) or (B) for onshore handling by EOD 29 May, we will start the run and deliver the PoC evidence bundle by EOD 31 May.
- Draft addendum / acceptance form: I will prepare a short addendum that lists the acceptance items above and the 48-hour review window. I'll circulate via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/some/docusign-link/ZX-4492

Please confirm the track and the exact object set for deletion. If accepted, we'll proceed and send the bundle + signed attestation at completion.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
